zod.dev:3: Primitive type schemas in Zod. z.string, z.number, z.bigint, z.boolean, z.symbol, z.undefined, z.null. Type coercion variants: z.coerce.string, z.coerce.number, z.coerce.boolean, z.coerce.bigint using String(), Number(), Boolean(), BigInt() constructors. Input type narrowing with generic parameters for coercion schemas.
zod.dev:5: Literal type schemas representing exact string, number, bigint, or boolean values. z.literal for single values. Multiple literals with array syntax. z.null and z.undefined for JavaScript literals. z.void equivalent to z.undefined. .values property to extract allowed values (Zod only).
zod.dev:6: String validation methods. Length constraints: .max, .min, .length, .nonempty (alias for .min(1)). Pattern matching: .regex, .startsWith, .endsWith, .includes. Case transformation: .uppercase, .lowercase. Other: .trim, .toLowerCase, .toUpperCase, .normalize for Unicode. Length measured in Unicode code points, not UTF-16.
zod.dev:7: String format validation schemas. Email: z.email with pattern parameter and built-in regexes (email, html5Email, rfc5322Email, unicodeEmail). UUID: z.uuid with version parameter (v1-v8), z.uuidv4, z.uuidv6, z.uuidv7, z.guid for non-RFC UUIDs. URLs: z.url with hostname/protocol regex, z.httpUrl for HTTP/HTTPS only. Hostname, E.164 phone, emoji (single character), base64, base64url, hex, JWT, nanoid, cuid, cuid2, ulid. IP: z.ipv4, z.ipv6, z.cidrv4, z.cidrv6 for CIDR notation. MAC: z.mac with 48-bit IEEE 802 format, delimiter parameter. Credit card: 12-19 digits with Luhn checksum. Currency: ISO 4217 codes. IBAN: 2-letter country, 2 check digits, 11-30 alphanumeric with ISO 7064 MOD 97-10 checksum. Hash: z.hash('md5','sha1','sha256','sha384','sha512') with enc parameter (hex/base64/base64url). ISO datetime/date/time/duration. Custom formats: z.stringFormat.
zod.dev:24: Template literal schemas introduced in zod@4.0. z.templateLiteral for dynamic string type definitions. Accepts string literals and schemas returning string|number|bigint|boolean|null|undefined. Supports unions from enum combinations.
zod.dev:25: Number validation schemas using z.number for finite numbers (rejects NaN, Infinity). Methods: .gt, .gte (alias .min), .lt, .lte (alias .max), .positive (alias .gt(0)), .nonnegative, .negative, .nonpositive, .multipleOf (alias .step). z.nan for NaN-only validation. Aliases .step for .multipleOf.
zod.dev:26: Integer validation. z.int restricts to safe integer range. z.int32 restricts to 32-bit range.
zod.dev:27: BigInt validation schemas using z.bigint. Supports same constraint methods as numbers: .gt, .gte (.min), .lt, .lte (.max), .positive (.gt(0n)), .nonnegative, .negative, .nonpositive, .multipleOf (.step).
zod.dev:28: Boolean validation using z.boolean for true/false values.
zod.dev:29: Date validation using z.date for Date instances. Rejects string dates. Custom error messages. Methods: .min and .max for date ranges. Zod Mini uses .check with z.minimum/z.maximum.
zod.dev:30: Enum schemas using z.enum for fixed string values. Accepts string arrays, object literals, TypeScript enums. Properties: .enum returns enum-like object (Zod only, Zod Mini uses .def.entries). Methods: .exclude to create subset excluding values (Zod only), .extract to create subset including values (Zod only).
zod.dev:34: Stringbool schemas introduced in zod@4.0. z.stringbool parses string 'boolish' values to boolean. Default truthy: ['true','1','yes','on','y','enabled']. Default falsy: ['false','0','no','off','n','disabled']. Case-insensitive by default. Custom truthy/falsy arrays. Case sensitivity with case: 'sensitive' parameter.
zod.dev:35: Optional schemas allowing undefined inputs. z.optional or .optional method. Returns ZodOptional wrapper. .unwrap extracts inner schema (Zod only, Zod Mini uses .def.innerType). .exactOptional for exactOptionalPropertyTypes behavior - absent key without explicit undefined.
zod.dev:36: Nullable schemas allowing null inputs. z.nullable or .nullable method. Returns ZodNullable wrapper. .unwrap extracts inner schema (Zod only, Zod Mini uses .def.innerType).
zod.dev:37: Nullish schemas combining optional and nullable (allows both null and undefined). z.nullish for both conditions.
zod.dev:38: Special types for unknown/any values. z.any allows any value (inferred type: any). z.unknown allows any value (inferred type: unknown). As object properties, both require the key to exist (use .optional for true optionality).
zod.dev:39: Never type schema. z.never rejects all values. No value will pass validation.
zod.dev:40: Object schemas with z.object for property definitions. Default: all properties required. Strictness: z.object (strips unknown keys), z.strictObject (rejects unknown keys), z.looseObject (allows unknown keys). Methods: .shape to access inner schemas, .keyof to create enum from keys, .extend to add fields, .safeExtend for type-safe extension, .pick to select keys, .omit to remove keys, .partial to make fields optional, .exactPartial for exactOptionalPropertyTypes, z.deepPartial for recursive optionality, .required to make fields required. Symbol keys with unique symbols and type tracking.
zod.dev:55: Recursive object types using getter syntax for lazy evaluation. Supports mutually recursive types. Cyclical inputs handled natively (Zod) or with z.memoizer registration (Zod Mini). Type inference errors resolved with type annotations on getters. Avoid nesting function calls and object-only recursion for best results.
zod.dev:57: Array schemas using z.array for homogeneous arrays. .unwrap extracts element schema (Zod only, Zod Mini uses .def.element). Constraints: .nonempty (minimum 1 item), .min(n), .max(n), .length(n).
zod.dev:58: Tuple schemas for fixed-length heterogeneous arrays with different schemas per index. z.tuple accepts array of schemas. Variadic rest argument: z.tuple([schema1], schema2) for [schema1, ...schema2[]]. .partial makes elements optional (Zod only). .exactPartial for exactOptionalPropertyTypes behavior.
zod.dev:59: Union schemas for 'OR' logic validating against multiple options. z.union checks options in order, returns first valid match. .options property extracts option schemas (Zod only, Zod Mini uses .def.options).
zod.dev:60: Exclusive unions (XOR) with z.xor requiring exactly one option to match. Fails if zero or multiple options match. Result has inclusive: false property with matches array. Object overlap detected (z.object strips keys); use .strict() to enforce mutual exclusivity.
zod.dev:61: Discriminated unions with z.discriminatedUnion(discriminatorKey, [options]) for type narrowing. Uses discriminator key for efficient parsing (faster than naive z.union). Each option should be object schema with discriminator as z.literal, z.enum, z.null, or z.undefined. Supports nesting. z.getDiscriminatedOption(schema, value) retrieves single option.
zod.dev:63: Intersection schemas for 'AND' logic combining type constraints. z.intersection represents A & B. Useful for intersecting objects; prefer .extend() over intersections for object merging (lacks methods like .pick, .omit).
zod.dev:64: Record schemas for key-value mappings Record<string,T>. z.record(keySchema, valueSchema) with keys assignable to string|number|symbol. Numeric keys validated as numeric strings. Default: exhaustiveness check for z.enum keys; use z.partialRecord to skip. z.looseRecord passes through non-matching keys. Value schema with .default, .prefault, .optional makes key optional on input.
zod.dev:68: Map schemas for JavaScript Map<K,V> validation. z.map(keySchema, valueSchema). Constraints: .nonempty (minimum 1 item), .min(n), .max(n), .size(n). Zod Mini uses .check(z.minSize/z.maxSize/z.size).
zod.dev:69: Set schemas for JavaScript Set<T> validation. z.set(elementSchema). Constraints: .nonempty (minimum 1 item), .min(n), .max(n), .size(n). Zod Mini uses .check(z.minSize/z.maxSize/z.size).
zod.dev:70: File schemas for File instance validation. z.file with methods: .min(bytes), .max(bytes) for size constraints, .mime(type) or .mime([types]) for MIME type validation. Zod Mini uses .check(z.minSize/z.maxSize/z.mime).
zod.dev:71: Promise schemas (deprecated). z.promise validates Promise instances. Validation in two parts: sync Promise check, async attach validation to .then. Use .parseAsync/.safeParseAsync for async resolution. Not recommended; await before parsing instead.
zod.dev:72: Instanceof schemas for class validation. z.instanceof(Class) checks class membership, returns exact object passed (no cloning). Works with built-in classes (RegExp, URL, Error). Methods: z.property(key, schema) for single property validation, z.properties(shape) for multiple properties (Zod) or spread syntax. .properties method on z.instanceof narrows inferred type.
zod.dev:75: Custom validation with refinements for logic not covered by native APIs. .refine(fn) for custom checks returning truthy/falsy. Error customization: error string or function. Abort flag: abort: true stops on failure. Path parameter customizes error location. Async refinements with async functions (requires .parseAsync). .when for conditional refinement execution. .superRefine for multiple issues with full control. .check (low-level API) for manual issue creation and control flow.
zod.dev:83: Codecs introduced in zod@4.1 for bidirectional transformations. z.codec(inputSchema, outputSchema, {decode, encode}) transforms between types. .decode (forward), .encode (backward). z.invertCodec swaps directions. Useful for network boundary conversions between JSON-friendly and rich JavaScript representations.
zod.dev:84: Pipe schemas chaining multiple schemas. z.pipe(schemaA, schemaB) validates input with A then passes to B. Syntax: schemaA.pipe(schemaB). z.input(schema) and z.output(schema) replace pipes for reaching nested codecs (works inside objects, records, maps).
zod.dev:86: Transform schemas for unidirectional transformations accepting any input and transforming output. z.transform(fn) with optional ctx for custom error reporting returning z.NEVER on error. Async transforms with async functions. .transform() convenience method. .preprocess(fn, schema) transforms input before validation. Useful for coercion, normalization, derivation.
zod.dev:89: Default values for schemas. .default(value) eagerly returns value if input undefined. .default(fn) re-executes function on each parse. Must be assignable to output type (short-circuits parsing).
zod.dev:90: Prefault values ('pre-parse defaults'). .prefault(value) returns value for undefined input but passes through parsing (not short-circuited). Must be assignable to input type. Useful for transforms and refinements on default values.
zod.dev:91: Catch fallback values for validation errors. .catch(value) returns fallback on validation failure. .catch(fn) re-executes function on each error. Function receives ctx with error and input (Zod Mini) or error object (Zod).
zod.dev:92: Branded types for nominal typing simulation in structural TypeScript. .brand<'BrandName'>() attaches brand to type. Requires parsing to create branded values (static-only construct). Second generic parameter for direction: .brand<'Name','out'> (output branded, default), .brand<'Name','in'> (input branded), .brand<'Name','inout'> (both branded). Requires Zod 4.2+.
zod.dev:93: Readonly schemas marking structures as immutable. .readonly or z.readonly(schema). Inferred type marked Readonly. Applies to objects, arrays, tuples, Set, Map. Uses Object.freeze to prevent runtime modifications. RuntimeError thrown on modification attempts.
zod.dev:94: JSON schema for JSON-encodable values. z.json convenience API expanding to union of string, number, boolean, null, array, object with recursive definitions.
zod.dev:95: Function schemas for Zod-validated function definitions. z.function({input: [schemas], output: schema}) with input as array or ZodTuple. Methods: .implement(fn) returns validated function, .implementAsync for async functions. Input-only validation: omit output field. Validates inputs/outputs, throws ZodError on failure.
zod.dev:96: Custom schemas for third-party or unsupported types. z.custom<T>(validationFn) with optional error message. No validation if no function provided (dangerous). Error customization like .refine. Prefer z.instanceof for class instances, z.templateLiteral for template types.
zod.dev:97: Apply method for incorporating external functions into schema chain. .apply(fn) calls function with schema. Additional arguments passed through. Enables composition of external validation logic.
zod.dev:98: Type matching utility z.toZod<T>() ensuring schema output type exactly matches T. Returns schema unchanged after validation. Exact type equality check (errors on drift). Alternative to satisfies z.ZodType<T>. Enum targets stay nominal - plain literal unions don't satisfy.

zod.dev:101: Data parsing with .parse method validating input and returning strongly-typed deep clone. .parseAsync for async refinements/transforms. Note: async schemas require .parseAsync, synchronous .parse throws error.
zod.dev:102: Error handling for validation failures. .parse throws ZodError instance. ZodError.issues array with granular information: expected type, code (invalid_type), path, message. .safeParse returns discriminated union {success: false, error: ZodError} or {success: true, data: T}. .safeParseAsync for async error handling. .validate returns boolean (never builds error, up to 16x faster than .safeParse().success). .validateAsync for async schemas with validation.
zod.dev:103: Type inference extracting static types from schemas. z.infer<typeof schema> extracts output type. z.input<typeof schema> extracts input type. z.output<typeof schema> equivalent to z.infer. Used for divergent input/output types with transforms. Links to full schema API documentation.

zod.dev:109: How encoding works in Zod schemas and codec subtypes. Codecs encapsulate bidirectional transformations with decode and encode functions. Pipes chain schemas (forward: A→B, backward: B→A). Refinements execute both directions. Transforms are unidirectional (error if encountered during encode). Stringbool internally implemented as codec. Defaults/prefaults and .catch only apply forward. Mutating transforms (.trim, .toLowerCase) work both directions.
zod.dev:117: Commonly-needed codec implementations. stringToNumber (parseFloat), stringToInt (parseInt), stringToBigInt (BigInt), numberToBigInt. Date conversions: isoDatetimeToDate, epochSecondsToDate, epochMillisToDate. JSON parsing with error handling. Byte conversions: utf8ToBytes, bytesToUtf8, base64ToBytes, base64urlToBytes, hexToBytes. URL: stringToURL, stringToHttpURL. URI component encoding/decoding. All provided as copy/paste implementations for customization.
zod.dev:134:
Ahead-of-time (AOT) compilation for Zod schemas producing hyperoptimized flat loop-free validators running several times faster than standard parser. Identical results and errors. Compilation of schema into JavaScript snippet via new Function(). 5x-7.8x speedup for container schemas (objects, tuples). Entire test suite runs twice - compiled and uncompiled - for perfect fidelity.
- z.compile(schema) compiles single schema returning compiled copy
- import 'zod/compile' global compilation mode (lazy, per-parse)
- Node.js CLI flags: --import zod/compile (ESM) or --require zod/compile (CommonJS)
- Compilation produces flat loop-free JavaScript using typeof checks
- new Function() generates fast-path validator code
- INVALID symbol signals fallback to uncompiled parser for errors
- Unsupported: async refinements, z.xor, recursive schemas, z.coerce.*, custom when, .catch callbacks
- Content Security Policy: z.config({jitless: true}) disables compilation
- Bundle size: compiler adds 7 KB gzipped (28 KB minified)
- Speedup ratios: 5-key object 1.8x, 20-key object 5.0x, 50-key object 10.2x

- When should I use z.compile?
- What schemas can be compiled?

zod.dev:135: z.compile() API for compiling single schema. Methods deriving new schemas (.refine, .extend, .optional, .meta) return uncompiled. Compile final schema, not intermediate results. Original schema unchanged. Returns compiled copy ready to use like normal schema.
zod.dev:136: Global compilation via import 'zod/compile' (must precede schema definitions). Enables automatic lazy compilation on first parse. Also works as Node.js CLI flag (--import zod/compile for ESM, --require for CommonJS) guaranteeing execution before modules define schemas. Preload in bunfig.toml or nub.jsonc. For applications only, not libraries.
zod.dev:137: How compilation works: walks entire schema producing hyperoptimized flat loop-free JavaScript via new Function(). No interpreter overhead, straight-line typeof checks and property reads. Generated code for Point example and Player schema. Uses INVALID symbol for fast-path validation failure to trigger standard parser fallback. Refinements and transforms execute once on valid input, at most twice on invalid.
zod.dev:138: Unsupported schemas and features. Can't compile: async refinements/transforms/checks, z.xor, recursive schemas, z.coerce.*, custom when parameter, .catch with callback (constants compile normally). Inside containers (object/array/tuple/record/intersection), unsupported children fall back to standard parser while structure stays compiled. Union with unsupported member, async anywhere, or .catch callback makes entire schema fall back. Pass strict: true to throw ZodCompileAsyncError or ZodCompileUnsupportedError.
zod.dev:139: Content Security Policy and jitless environments. new Function disabled in CSP/no-eval. Global mode respects jitless setting: z.config({jitless: true}). Direct z.compile() call is explicit opt-in attempting generation regardless of jitless (returns uncompiled in restricted environments).
zod.dev:140: Bundle size impact: compiler adds ~7 KB gzipped (28 KB minified). Without z.compile() or 'zod/compile' import, compiler tree-shaken completely. Zod 24.1 KB → 31.1 KB with compiler, Zod Mini 4.6 KB → 13.2 KB with compiler.
zod.dev:141: Performance benchmarks for compilation speedup. Single-schema tight loop results: 5-key object 1.8x, 10-key 2.2x, 20-key 5.0x, 50-key 10.2x faster. Tuple: 1-item 2.2x, 3-item 2.5x, 5-item 3.0x, 10-item 3.7x. Moltar benchmark: Zod compiled 47.5M ops/sec (parseSafe), Zod compiled 60.6M (assertLoose).

zod.dev:186: Conversion details. zod.dev:216: $ZodIssue objects extend $ZodIssueBase interface with code (string), input (unknown), path (PropertyKey array), message (string). zod.dev:217: Zod Mini tree-shakable variant of Zod with functional API. Import from zod/mini or @zod/mini standalone package. Same functionality as regular Zod but using functions instead of methods for tree-shaking. Example: z.nullable(z.optional(z.string())) vs z.string().optional().nullable(). Bundle size reduction: 64% smaller for simple boolean parse (2.12kb vs 5.91kb gzipped). Tree-shaking removes unused code; bundlers cannot remove unused methods but can remove unused functions. Use cases: frontend with slow mobile connections. Not recommended for backend or if bundle size < 10kb not significant. Less discoverable DX than regular Zod. Base class ZodMiniType extends core.$ZodType. Questions: What is Zod Mini? How much smaller is bundle? When should I use Zod Mini? What checks are available? What methods does ZodMiniType have?
zod.dev:218: Tree-shaking or dead-code elimination. Regular Zod schemas provide convenience methods bundlers cannot remove. Zod Mini uses top-level functions which bundlers can tree-shake. Example regular Zod: z.string().min(5).max(10).trim() becomes z.string().check(z.minLength(5), z.maxLength(10), z.trim()). Bundle sizes: simple boolean parse with Zod Mini 2.12kb gzipped vs Zod 5.91kb (64% reduction). Object schema with Zod Mini 4.0kb vs Zod 13.1kb (69% reduction). Provides understanding of relative bundle sizes.
zod.dev:219: Use regular Zod unless very strict bundle size constraints. Bundle size on scale of Zod (5-10kb) only meaningful for frontend optimizing for slow mobile in rural/developing areas. Backend development: bundle size not meaningful even on Lambda - 17kb gzipped Zod adds only ~0.6ms cold start. DX: Mini API more verbose, less discoverable, harder to discover methods via Intellisense than chained APIs. Cannot quickly build schemas with chained methods. Internet speed: round trip to server (100-200ms) dwells download time for 10kb. Only on slow 3G (sub-1Mbps) does extra 10kb become significant.

zod.dev:231: Zod 4 migration guide and release notes. Breaking changes listed from highest to lowest impact. Install zod@^4.0.0. Error customization APIs unified under `error` parameter replacing deprecated message, invalid_type_error, required_error, errorMap. ZodError changes: issue formats streamlined, error map precedence changed, .format() and .flatten() deprecated for z.treeifyError(), .formErrors and .errors removed, .addIssue(s) deprecated. Type-specific changes: z.number() no infinite values, .int() safe integers only, z.string() formats as top-level functions, UUID stricter, base64url no padding. z.coerce input type unknown, missing keys error. .default() short-circuits on undefined (vs Zod 3 parsing), .prefault() for pre-parse default. z.object() defaults applied in optional fields, .strict()/.passthrough() deprecated for strictObject/looseObject, .merge() deprecated for .extend(), z.unknown/any required. z.array().nonempty() type changed, z.promise() deprecated. z.function() result no longer Zod schema, uses input/output, implements/implementAsync. .refine() ignores type predicates, ctx.path removed. Release notes: 14x faster strings, 7x faster arrays, 6.5x faster objects, 100x reduction in tsc instantiations, 57% smaller bundle (Zod 4 vs 3), 85% smaller with Zod Mini. New features: metadata registries, JSON Schema conversion, recursive objects, file schemas, internationalization, template literals, number formats (int32, uint32, int64, uint64, float32, float64), stringbool, discriminated union improvements, multi-value literals, refinements in schemas, .overwrite() method.
zod.dev:232: Error customization APIs unified under error parameter. Replaces message parameter (deprecated but still supported). Drops invalid_type_error and required_error - use error parameter with issue.input check instead. Drops errorMap renamed to error. Error functions can return plain string (not {message: string}), or undefined to yield to next error map. Supports error: function(issue) pattern.
zod.dev:236: ZodError issue formats streamlined. Issue subtypes: $ZodIssueInvalidType, $ZodIssueTooBig, $ZodIssueTooSmall, $ZodIssueInvalidStringFormat, $ZodIssueNotMultipleOf, $ZodIssueUnrecognizedKeys, $ZodIssueInvalidValue, $ZodIssueInvalidUnion, $ZodIssueInvalidKey (new), $ZodIssueInvalidElement (new), $ZodIssueCustom. Old types removed/merged. All issues conform to $ZodIssueBase interface. Error map precedence changed - schema-level error maps take precedence over .parse() error maps. .format() and .flatten() methods deprecated for z.treeifyError(). .formErrors removed. .errors alias removed, use .issues. .addIssue(s) deprecated, push to issues array instead.
zod.dev:244: z.number() changes: no infinite values (POSITIVE_INFINITY/NEGATIVE_INFINITY invalid), .safe() deprecated behaves like .int() no longer accepts floats, .int() accepts safe integers only within Number.MIN_SAFE_INTEGER to Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER range.
zod.dev:248: z.string() updates: email, uuid, url, etc. moved to top-level functions (z.email(), z.uuid(), z.url(), z.emoji(), z.base64(), z.base64url(), z.nanoid(), z.cuid(), z.cuid2(), z.ulid(), z.ipv4(), z.ipv6(), z.cidrv4(), z.cidrv6(), z.iso.date(), z.iso.time(), z.iso.datetime(), z.iso.duration()). zod.dev:255: z.coerce updates: input type now unknown (was string for coerce.string). Missing key on object with coerce field now errors - use .default() to declare fallback. Example: z.coerce.boolean() on missing key throws instead of defaulting to false.
zod.dev:256: .default() behavior changed: if input undefined, short-circuits and returns default value (must be assignable to output type). Zod 3 parsed default value against input type. z.prefault() (pre-parse default) replicates Zod 3 behavior - parses default value before returning.
zod.dev:257: z.object() changes: defaults applied within optional fields (Zod 3 had defaults not apply in optional), .strict() and .passthrough() deprecated for z.strictObject() and z.looseObject() functions, .strict() and .passthrough() remain for backwards compatibility, .strip() deprecated (was default behavior), .nonstrict() long-deprecated removed, .deepPartial() removed (deprecated in v3), z.unknown() and z.any() no longer key optional in inferred types, parse-time check added (v4.4.0+), use .optional() for key that may be absent, .merge() deprecated for .extend() (better TypeScript performance), .extend() preferred with .shape destructuring syntax.
zod.dev:265: z.nativeEnum() deprecated in favor of z.enum(). z.enum() overloaded to support enum-like input. z.enum(Color) accepts native enums. ColorSchema.enum.Red canonical API. ColorSchema.Enum and ColorSchema.Values removed.
zod.dev:266: z.array() changes: .nonempty() type changed - now behaves like .min(1) with inferred type string[] (not [string, ...string[]]). Old behavior use z.tuple([z.string()], z.string()) for [string, ...string[]] type.
zod.dev:268: z.promise() deprecated. Rarely necessary - await before parsing with Zod. z.function() removed need for z.promise() in async functions.
zod.dev:269: z.function() no longer Zod schema. Acts as standalone function factory. API changed: upfront input/output schemas instead of .args() and .returns() methods. Syntax: z.function({input: [...], output: ...}). .implement() and .implementAsync() methods for defining functions. .implementAsync() for async functions.
zod.dev:271: .refine() changes: ignores type predicates (type narrowing no longer works), drops ctx.path (not eagerly evaluated), drops function as second argument pattern. Use error parameter instead for custom messages.
zod.dev:275: z.ostring(), z.onumber(), etc. undocumented convenience methods removed.
zod.dev:276: z.literal() drops symbol support (symbols not literal values, not comparable with ===).
zod.dev:278: Static .create() factories dropped (z.ZodString.create()). Use standalone factory functions instead.
zod.dev:279: z.record() changes: drops single argument usage (z.record(z.string()) invalid), requires two arguments z.record(z.string(), z.string()). Improves enum support: z.record(z.enum(['a','b','c']), z.number()) now exhaustive {a: number; b: number; c: number} not partial. z.partialRecord() for optional keys.
zod.dev:282: z.intersection() throws regular Error on merge conflict (Zod 3 threw ZodError with invalid_intersection_types issue). Unmergable results indicate structural schema problem not validation error.
zod.dev:284: Internal changes: ZodType generics changed from <Output, Def, Input=Output> to <Output=unknown, Input=unknown>, Def generic removed. Input defaults to unknown not Output. z.ZodTypeAny eliminated, use z.ZodType. z.core subpackage added for shared utilities. ._def moved to ._zod.def. ZodEffects dropped - refinements live in schemas, stored in checks array. ZodTransform added for transforms. ZodPreprocess dropped, z.preprocess() returns ZodPipe. ZodBranded dropped, branding via direct type modification.
